if: the inward supply is a MOTOR VEHICLE FOR TRANSPORTATION OF PERSONS with approved seating capacity of NOT MORE THAN THIRTEEN persons, including the driver
AND it is NOT used for making any of these taxable supplies: (A) further supply of such motor vehicles, (B) transportation of passengers, or (C) imparting training on driving such motor vehicles
then: input tax credit is NOT AVAILABLE on that motor vehicle
note: The seating test is 'approved seating capacity', INCLUDING the driver, and the threshold is thirteen — a fourteen-seat vehicle is outside this clause. The clause covers vehicles for transportation of PERSONS only; goods vehicles are not caught. The three exceptions are exhaustive and each is a taxable supply the claimant must actually make: owning a car and occasionally carrying a client is not 'transportation of passengers'. Section 17(5) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 16 and sub-section (1) of section 18', so this block defeats both the s.16(1) entitlement and the s.18(1) special-circumstances credit. Business use does not cure it. The source is the CGST Act as updated 31-08-2021. UNKNOWN whether a later amendment has changed this clause; later amendments are not held locally.
